# Supermatter Crystal
## Overview
The Supermatter Crystal is an advanced crystalline material capable of converting applied energy and structural stress into multiple useful outputs.
Unlike conventional generators, the Supermatter does not produce electrical power directly. Instead, energy is harvested from the reactions caused by controlled interaction with the crystal.
The exact mechanisms behind Supermatter behaviour remain partially unknown. Current research indicates that the crystal interacts with environmental conditions and external energy sources in complex ways.
## Power Harvesting
Controlled Supermatter stress allows engineers to harvest energy from the resulting reactions.
One observed reaction produces high-energy radiation.
Radiation collectors convert this emitted radiation into usable electrical power.
Another observed reaction involves the accumulation of electrical charge within the crystal.
Tesla coils allow this stored electrical energy to be transferred into the station power network.
## Gas Harvesting
Supermatter reactions also produce gaseous byproducts.
Damaged or stressed crystal material releases oxygen and tritium as part of its structural decomposition process.
These gases can be collected and processed for station use, providing Atmospherics with a continuous supply of valuable resources.
## Minimal Operating Standards
A stable Supermatter installation must maintain:
- Active cooling - Overpressure prevention measures - Continuous atmospheric supply
Failure to maintain these conditions represents a significant risk to station safety.
Standard atmospheric conditions have been observed to provide a stable operating environment. Alterations should only be performed with appropriate justification and careful consideration.
